methodology_note_latency: IMPORTANT: the extractor's `latency_ms` field measures wall time starting BEFORE the 5-RPM self-throttle wait (utils.rate_limiter.wait_for_rate_limit, called inside nlu/extractor.py::_invoke_cerebras_json before each POST). On the official pilot run this produced ~12,000ms per case (7 of 8), which is almost entirely OUR OWN rate-limit wait (token bucket refill ~12s at 5 RPM, capacity=1), not model latency - confirmed by a follow-up diagnostic pass that measured (a) pure requests.post() round-trip time and (b) the provider's own `time_info.total_time`/`queue_time`/`prompt_time`/`completion_time` fields, both timed AFTER the rate-limit wait had already elapsed. This is a measurement artifact of Free-Trial-tier throttling, not a property of the model's inference speed, and is corrected below. The Free Trial's 5 RPM cap is a temporary account-tier limit (paid Developer tier has materially higher RPM per the provider verification doc), so uncorrected wall-clock-including-throttle numbers would misrepresent this candidate for the architectural latency question this experiment exists to answer.

hard_rejection_gate_assessment.gate: Step 3 - reject immediately on any SYSTEMIC defect, skip full dev
hard_rejection_gate_assessment.engineering_judgment: REJECT. The generic-intent-collapse pattern (2/8 cases, both distinct gold classes collapsing into the identical predicted class A_literature_evidence, concentrated in exactly the two hardest/most reasoning-dependent categories) is explicitly named in the task's own gate language as the disqualifying pattern to watch for ('multiple different question types all collapsing to the same predicted intent'). At n=8 the absolute count is small and could partly be sampling noise, but (a) it recurs across two structurally different query types rather than being a single fluke, (b) it correlates directly with a secondary failure (required_sources under-coverage) in both of the same two cases, and (c) it has an identifiable, non-fixable-within-scope root cause: reasoning_effort='low' is the genuine lowest officially-supported setting on this model, and raising it to medium/high (the only lever that would plausibly fix multi-hop/ambiguity reasoning) would reintroduce the reasoning-token latency burn this experiment exists to eliminate - there is no mechanical prompt/schema fix available under the Step 6 bounded-adaptation allowance (which explicitly excludes tuning away a fundamental semantic-behavior problem). All other candidate-disqualifying patterns (B/G confusion, catastrophic entity loss, entity mistyping, fabricated IDs, major constraint loss, broad false ambiguity, semantic_roles regression, semantically-empty-valid outputs, normalization corruption, unsupported field invention) were NOT observed. This is a narrower, less severe failure than candidate_e_nvidia_fast's 5/8 collapse, but it is the same failure class, and quality has explicit priority over latency per the task's decision rule.
